## Purpose and workspace
Serde is a Rust serialization/deserialization framework. This Cargo workspace separates stable public traits, the user-facing facade, compile-time derives, and validation. Workspace definition: `Cargo.toml`.

## Public API facade
The `serde` crate is the normal consumer entry point. It re-exports core APIs and conditionally integrates derive support, while retaining compatibility-oriented code such as 128-bit integer handling. Primary paths: `serde/src/lib.rs`, `serde/src/core`, `serde/src/integer128.rs`.

## Format-agnostic serialization contract
`serde_core` defines the format-independent boundary between Rust data types and external format crates: `Serialize` drives values into a format-provided `Serializer`; `Deserialize` reconstructs values through a format-provided `Deserializer` and visitors. Implementations for standard Rust types live alongside these contracts. Paths: `serde_core/src/ser/mod.rs`, `serde_core/src/de/mod.rs`, `serde_core/src/lib.rs`.

## Value traversal and error boundary
Serialization is controlled by the data type’s `Serialize` implementation; deserialization is controlled by the format parser plus Serde’s `Visitor`/seed protocol. Formats own concrete wire representations, parsers, output buffers, and error types; Serde owns generic structural traversal and trait contracts. In-memory deserialization utilities and ignored-value support are provided in: `serde_core/src/de/value.rs`, `serde_core/src/de/ignored_any.rs`, `serde_core/src/ser/impls.rs`.

## Derive macro compiler pipeline
`serde_derive` is a procedural-macro crate invoked by Rust compilation for `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]`. It parses a struct/enum and Serde attributes into an internal AST, validates representation and attribute constraints, computes generic bounds/names, then emits trait implementations for serialization and deserialization. Entry and stages: `serde_derive/src/lib.rs`, `serde_derive/src/internals/ast.rs`, `serde_derive/src/internals/check.rs`.

## Generated implementation strategies
Macro generation has distinct serializer and deserializer pipelines. Deserialization generation branches by container shape and enum representation—external, internal, adjacent, and untagged tags—while serialization emits corresponding structural calls into `Serializer`. Paths: `serde_derive/src/ser.rs`, `serde_derive/src/de.rs`, `serde_derive/src/de/enum_.rs`.

## Runtime, integration, and delivery
This is a Rust library workspace, not an application or service. Consumer applications supply data-format crates (for example `serde_json`); those external crates implement Serde’s serializer/deserializer interfaces. The repository targets standard Rust and constrained/no-std environments, with a no-std integration target at `test_suite/no_std/Cargo.toml`. GitHub Actions provides CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
